### What is constrained?

$$
\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma,\qquad
\gamma\gamma_{\mathrm{EBL}}\to e^+e^-,\qquad
e^\pm\gamma_{\mathrm{bg}}\to e^\pm\gamma
$$

Escaping high-energy photons feed a lower-energy electromagnetic cascade.

| Input | Constraint |
|:---|:---|
| Measured neutrino spectrum | Pion production and its energy dependence |
| Fermi isotropic gamma-ray background | A ceiling on the accompanying extragalactic cascade |
| Internal photon absorption | Redistribution of photon energy before escape |

Other source populations also contribute to the gamma-ray background.

::::::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** Wherever neutrinos are made, gamma rays are made too. On the way to us they cascade to lower energies — and the measured gamma-ray background leaves little room for them.

Spend about 90 seconds; this returns from the Galaxy to the extragalactic diffuse
spectrum shown two slides earlier. Read the
figure from right to left: neutrino measurements fix a pion-production
scale; escaped photons cascade and contribute to the Fermi IGRB. Grey points
are IceCube (the published Combined Fit segmented flux times three, all flavours,
as in the original), violet Fermi. Dashed curves fit neutrinos; solid curves and
bands are model photon predictions. White is a single power law continued to
1 TeV, orange a broken power law, blue a log parabola. The redraw is digitized
from the original raster; band edges hidden under the original legend (below
about 7e-10 GeV cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1) are not recovered, so the redrawn y axis stops
there. Colour marks the spectral model, line style what is drawn (dashed:
neutrino fit, solid: cascade photons). As drawn in the source, the dashed single power law lies about 15%
above the IceCube Combined Fit SPL normalization.

The benchmark assumes gamma-transparent extragalactic sources, star-formation-rate
redshift evolution and K_pi approximately 1 for p-gamma. The earlier pp coefficient
3/2 must not be transferred to this figure. Bands combine spectral-fit and EBL
model uncertainties. The IGRB is a ceiling because other populations contribute.
Spectral suppression and internal reprocessing can ease the tension. Neither
this comparison nor the spectral break identifies a unique source population.
The Delta-resonance interpretation is a proposed model, not an experimental
identification of the break's origin.

Sources: [Zathul et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00249v2),
[Murase, Guetta & Ahlers (2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.00805).
:::

## Compact regions and hidden gamma rays {#hidden-sources}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### A compact AGN region

![](media/response/compact-source.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-width: 1200px; --media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="Causal diagram of a compact source: energetic protons meet gas or photons, pions produce neutrinos that escape and gamma rays that can be converted to electron-positron pairs and reprocessed photons. The diagram is schematic and has no calculated flux."}

$$
f_{pp}\simeq1-e^{-t_{\mathrm{res}}/t_{pp}},\qquad
t_{pp}^{-1}=\kappa_{pp}\,n_{\mathrm{gas}}\,\sigma_{pp}\,c
$$

::: {.media-caption}
Gas-target energy-loss estimate · Schematic geometry · [Murase & Stecker](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03381)
:::

### Photon opacity

$$
\gamma+\gamma\to e^++e^-,\qquad
E_\gamma\epsilon\gtrsim(m_ec^2)^2\quad\text{(head-on)}
$$

| Condition | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| Above pair-production threshold | Absorption is kinematically allowed |
| $\tau_{\gamma\gamma}\gtrsim1$ | Photon density and path length make it effective |
| Pair cooling and further interactions | Energy emerges at different photon energies |

Neutrino escape depends on the matter column as well.

::::::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** So the sources may be hidden: dense, compact regions where neutrinos escape, but gamma rays are absorbed and come out at much lower energies.

Spend about one minute on the diagram. It represents a class of compact gas/radiation
environments, such as an AGN corona, not a resolved image of NGC 1068. Acceleration
supplies the nonthermal protons; gas and photons are alternative pion-production
targets. The gas branch defines f_pp as an approximate energy-loss fraction for
a prescribed residence time, with constant effective kappa and cross section.
It is not the fraction of proton energy carried by neutrinos. Cooling, escape
and acceleration must be compared for a quantitative source model.

Gamma-gamma conversion requires both the threshold and sufficient optical depth.
The stated threshold uses a head-on collision and energies in one local frame.
Pairs radiate and can feed cascades; energy is redistributed rather than destroyed.
Emission can be quenched or shifted outside the observed high-energy band.
Neutrinos escape only for a sufficiently small neutrino interaction optical depth.
The diagram computes neither opacity, transport nor a neutrino luminosity.

Return to this mechanism when comparing the NGC 1068 photon/neutrino spectra.
Sources: [Murase & Stecker](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03381),
[IceCube NGC 1068 comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09972).
:::
